status: REFERENCE ONLY — no inference has been run on these cases. They define the ownership/scope and atomicity distinctions the v2 instrument must be able to score. They are not evidence about any model.
schema_note: Same required/forbidden schema as corpus.json, plus optional temporal_ids, attribution_forbidden, compound_ok, noise_markers and an ownership block. The ownership block is declarative: the evaluator cannot infer ownership from free text.

cases.conversation:
[user] Jim: "The king is a criminal. He sold the northern road to the guild."
[user] Lisa: "That's not true. The king is wonderful — he rebuilt the harbour after the flood."
[user] Bob: "I've served him twenty years. The king is honorable, whatever the rumours say."
[assistant] The three of them let the argument drop and drank.
cases.notes: Three incompatible beliefs about the same topic. None establishes the objective truth about the king. Correct behaviour is to keep three separate character-scoped beliefs (or store none), never one world fact.

cases.conversation:
[user] Jim (to Lisa, quietly): "The vault code is 4417. Don't tell Bob."
[user] Lisa: "I won't."
[assistant] Bob was across the room, studying the fire.
cases.notes: A disclosure with named recipients. Jim's private knowledge may become Lisa's knowledge; it must not become Bob's knowledge or an unattributed world fact. The conversation layer establishes the disclosure event and its recipients; the memory mechanism must not infer exposure.

cases.conversation:
[user] (scene: the harbour at low tide) The dockmaster says the tide gate jams every winter.
[assistant] The gate groaned somewhere below the pier.
[user] (scene change: the king's court, three weeks later) A herald announces the winter levy.
cases.notes: The tide-gate fact is true in the harbour scene. It must not silently migrate into a court-scene memory record as though it were a court fact.

cases.conversation: [user] Halden trained Sable as a cartographer at Ossary for nine years, and she still uses his compass.
cases.notes: Control for the atomicity rule: one subject, one event, several details. This must be judged a legitimate compound, not a merge of distinct facts. Splitting it is not required and is not penalised.
